## Task design {#explanation-of-the-task-2}

Task 2 examined whether participants could combine information about estimated voltage
and its uncertainty to locate a relevant spatial region. On each trial, participants saw
one EEG topoplot and were asked to select the scalp region with the highest
signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), defined as the absolute average-referenced voltage divided
by its standard error. They responded using a separate scalp layout divided into 64
selectable regions.

The task included three characteristic ERP patterns: MMN, P3, and N170. Each was shown
using each of the seven visualization types. This produced 21 trials per participant,
each on a separate page. Trial order was randomized separately for every participant.

![Example uncertainty-integration trial. Participants selected one of 64 regions after
identifying the region with the highest SNR.](<../The Art of Uncertain Topoplots/figures/task2_explainer_64_regions.png>){#fig-task2-explainer width=100% fig-alt="An example signal-to-noise-ratio topoplot beside a scalp selection grid divided into 64 regions. A pointer illustrates selecting one region on the grid."}

## Trial reconstruction and scoring {#response-scoring-and-trial-reconstruction}

- For each participant we reconstructed presentation order. Each participant went through 21 randomly shuffled pages.

- For each trial, survey recorded the visualization, ERP stimulus shown
  and one region selected by participant. There were 64 regions on selectable grid.

- The selected region was matched to the corresponding stimulus and its stored region score in `regions.txt`.

- The region score is the mean |voltage| / SE in that region, rescaled within each
  stimulus so that the weakest region scores 0 and the strongest 1. The steps are in the
  note below.

::: {.callout-note title="How the 0–1 region score was calculated" collapse="true"}

For each stimulus, the scoring pipeline performed the following steps:

1. It loaded one average-referenced ERP case using the task, subject, time point, and
   condition recorded in `task_configs_30_balanced`. The fixed combinations were:

   | ERP pattern | Time point (index) | Condition |
   |:------------|-------------------:|----------:|
   | MMN         |                 96 |         3 |
   | N170        |                105 |         2 |
   | P3          |                129 |         1 |

2. It average-referenced the voltage across the $N$ channels:

   $$
   V_i^{AR} = V_i - \frac{1}{N}\sum_j V_j.
   $$

3. It calculated a polarity-independent, t-like signal-to-noise value at each channel:

   $$
   T_i = \frac{|V_i^{AR}|}{SE_i}.
   $$

4. It interpolated the channel-level $T_i$ values into a continuous topoplot grid. Only
   finite interpolated cells inside the visible head mask were retained.

5. It fitted the saved 64-region polygon template to the topoplot domain. For each
   region $k$, it averaged all retained grid cells that were inside both the polygon and
   the head mask:

   $$
   R_k = \operatorname{mean}\{T(x,y):(x,y)\in\text{region}_k\}.
   $$

6. It min--max normalized the 64 raw region scores separately within each stimulus:

   $$
   S_k = \frac{R_k - \min_j R_j}{\max_j R_j - \min_j R_j}.
   $$

   The weakest region therefore receives 0, the strongest receives 1, and other regions
   are positioned proportionally between them. Scores are rounded to two decimal places.

**Implementation references.** The stimulus-generation source is stored under
`UnfoldMakie/experiments/working/`:

- stimulus selection: `stimuli_data.jl:213`;
- average referencing and channel score: `region_detection/rereferencing.jl:96`;
- topoplot interpolation: `region_detection/region_score_exports.jl:48`;
- polygon validation and fitting: `get_regions.jl:19`;
- regional averaging: `region_detection/scoring.jl:338`;
- normalization, rounding, and export: `region_detection/region_score_exports.jl:7`.

The polygon definitions are stored in
`experiments/figures/task2_topo_regions_64_eeg_aligned_pipeline28/regions.jl`.

## Observed detection scores {#descriptive-detection-scores}

- The analysis contains `r scales::comma(nrow(task2))` responses: `r n_distinct(task2$ID)`
  participants x `r n_distinct(task2$trial)` trials. Each visualization type therefore has
  `r scales::comma(nrow(task2) / n_distinct(task2$vistype))` responses:
  `r n_distinct(task2$ID)` participants x `r n_distinct(task2$pattern)` ERP patterns.

- `r scales::comma(sum(complete.cases(task2)))` of `r scales::comma(nrow(task2))` records
  contain participant, stimulus, visualization type, pattern, position, and score;
  `r sum(!complete.cases(task2))` were excluded for missing model variables.

- Visualization type was treated as a categorical variable, with Basic topoplot as the
  reference condition. ERP pattern and stimulus were retained for the extended model.

- Presentation position was represented by `position_c = position - 11`. Thus,
  `position_c = 0` represents position 11, negative values represent earlier trials, and
  positive values represent later trials.

```{r}
task2_model <- task2 %>%
  transmute(
    ID = factor(ID),
    stimulus = factor(stimulus),
    vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
    pattern = factor(pattern),
    position_c = as.integer(position) - 11,
    score = as.numeric(score)
  ) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

stimulus_pattern_counts <- task2_model |>
  distinct(stimulus, pattern) |>
  count(stimulus)

stopifnot(
  nrow(task2_model) == nrow(task2),
  all(stimulus_pattern_counts$n == 1)
)
```

### Cumulative distribution

```{r task2-score-ecdf}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Cumulative distribution of the ", scales::comma(nrow(task2_model)), " trial-level detection scores, one line per visualization (", scales::comma(nrow(task2_model) / n_distinct(task2_model$vistype)), " responses each). Each line gives the share of responses at or below a score; Basic topoplot in blue. The final jump at 100% is the share of responses that selected the strongest region. Legend entries follow the order used in all figures (Basic topoplot first).")
#| fig-alt: "Seven step lines of the cumulative share of responses against the detection score, one per visualization, rising slowly up to about 80% and then jumping to 100% at a score of 100%. The lines lie close together; Basic topoplot is drawn in blue."
# ECDF instead of the 0.01-bin histogram alone (audit V17e): no comb pattern, and
# the visualizations can be compared on one axis. The lines run close together, so
# end labels would collide; a legend inside the empty upper-left corner names them.
# Legend in the display order of every figure (audit V1), not in the order of the
# lines: the lines run close together, so the visualizations are found by name.
# Grey shades follow the legend, darkest first.
task2_ecdf_order <- levels(order_vistype(task2_model$vistype))
task2_ecdf_others <- setdiff(task2_ecdf_order, "basic")
task2_ecdf_colours <- c(
  basic = basic_accent,
  setNames(
    grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#252525", "#B0B0B0"))(length(task2_ecdf_others)),
    task2_ecdf_others
  )
)

task2_ecdf_data <- task2_model |>
  mutate(vistype = factor(as.character(vistype), levels = task2_ecdf_order))

task2_score_ecdf_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_ecdf_data,
  aes(x = score, colour = vistype)
) +
  # Grey lines first, Basic topoplot drawn on top.
  stat_ecdf(
    data = \(d) filter(d, vistype != "basic"),
    geom = "step",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  stat_ecdf(
    data = \(d) filter(d, vistype == "basic"),
    geom = "step",
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = task2_ecdf_colours,
    breaks = task2_ecdf_order,
    labels = figure_vistype,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    "Detection score (0% = weakest region, 100% = strongest region)",
    limits = c(-0.01, 1.01),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    "Share of responses (cumulative)",
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.3))) +
  # No in-figure title (one title per figure): the caption names the figure.
  plot_theme(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 20),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.02, 0.98),
    legend.justification = c(0, 1),
    legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "lines"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )

task2_score_ecdf_figure
```

### Histogram

```{r task2-score-distribution}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Distribution of the ", scales::comma(nrow(task2_model)), " trial-level detection scores. Bars show frequencies at the recorded score resolution of 1 percentage point. A score of 0% indicates selection of the weakest region for a stimulus, whereas 100% indicates selection of the strongest region. Intermediate values preserve graded performance.")

task2_score_distribution <- task2_model |>
  transmute(score_index = as.integer(round(score * 100))) |>
  count(score_index, name = "responses") |>
  tidyr::complete(
    score_index = 0:100,
    fill = list(responses = 0L)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    score = score_index / 100,
    score_type = if_else(
      score_index %in% c(0L, 100L),
      "Boundary score",
      "Intermediate score"
    ),
    percentage = 100 * responses / sum(responses),
    label_hjust = if_else(score_index == 0L, 0, 1)
  )

stopifnot(
  sum(task2_score_distribution$responses) == nrow(task2_model),
  all(task2_score_distribution$score >= 0),
  all(task2_score_distribution$score <= 1)
)

task2_score_distribution_figure <- ggplot(
  task2_score_distribution,
  aes(x = score, y = responses, fill = score_type)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.009) +
  geom_text(
    data = task2_score_distribution |>
      filter(score_index %in% c(0L, 100L)),
    aes(
      label = sprintf("n = %d (%.1f%%)", responses, percentage),
      hjust = label_hjust
    ),
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = 5,
    colour = "#111111",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Intermediate score" = "#6BAED6",
      "Boundary score" = "#08519C"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    "Detection score (0% = weakest region, 100% = strongest region)",
    limits = c(-0.01, 1.01),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    "Number of responses",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  # No in-figure title (one title per figure): the caption names the figure.
  plot_theme(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 20)
  )

task2_score_distribution_figure

ggsave_st(
  project_path("figures", "task2_score_distribution_figure.png"),
  task2_score_distribution_figure,
  width = 9,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 180,
  device = ragg::agg_png,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r task2-descriptive-setup}
#| include: false
# Data and shared layers for the Task 2 descriptive plots below (Ambiguation,
# Gradient, 95% CI whiskers), so the tabs can come in any order.
task2_gradient_participants <- task2_model |>
  group_by(ID, vistype) |>
  summarise(
    participant_score = mean(score),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

task2_gradient_summary <- task2_gradient_participants |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    n_participants = n(),
    mean_score = mean(participant_score),
    se_score = sd(participant_score) / sqrt(n_participants),
    df = n_participants - 1,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Rows in the display order of every figure (audit V1), Basic topoplot at the
    # top: y_position counts up from the bottom row.
    vistype = order_vistype(vistype, top_first = TRUE),
    y_position = as.numeric(vistype),
    lower_95 = mean_score - qt(0.975, df) * se_score,
    upper_95 = mean_score + qt(0.975, df) * se_score
  ) |>
  arrange(vistype)

task2_gradient_means <- setNames(
  task2_gradient_summary$mean_score,
  as.character(task2_gradient_summary$vistype)
)
task2_gradient_value <- function(vistype) {
  sprintf("%.2f", task2_gradient_means[[vistype]])
}
task2_gradient_difference <-
  task2_gradient_means[["triple_CI"]] -
  task2_gradient_means[["bivariate_corner"]]

stopifnot(
  all(
    task2_gradient_summary$n_participants ==
      n_distinct(task2_model$ID)
  )
)

# x range: the gradient fades out by about 3 SE from the mean, so the axis covers
# mean +/- 4 SE for every visualization, rounded outward to 0.05.
task2_gradient_limits <- c(
  floor(min(task2_gradient_summary$mean_score - 4 * task2_gradient_summary$se_score) / 0.05) * 0.05,
  ceiling(max(task2_gradient_summary$mean_score + 4 * task2_gradient_summary$se_score) / 0.05) * 0.05
)

task2_gradient_data <- task2_gradient_summary |>
  tidyr::crossing(score = seq(
    task2_gradient_limits[1],
    task2_gradient_limits[2],
    length.out = round(diff(task2_gradient_limits) * 800) + 1
  )) |>
  mutate(
    t_distance = abs(score - mean_score) / se_score,
    confidence_level = 2 * pt(t_distance, df) - 1,
    gradient_alpha = if_else(
      confidence_level <= 0.95,
      1,
      pmax(0, (1 - confidence_level) / 0.05)
    )
  )

task2_score_plot_layers <- function(mean_tick_colour = "#111111", mean_tick_half_height = 0.31) {
  list(
    geom_segment(
      data = task2_gradient_summary,
      aes(
        x = mean_score,
        xend = mean_score,
        y = y_position - mean_tick_half_height,
        yend = y_position + mean_tick_half_height
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.8,
      colour = mean_tick_colour
    ),
    geom_text(
      data = task2_gradient_summary,
      aes(
        x = mean_score,
        y = y_position + 0.42,
        label = scales::percent(mean_score, accuracy = 1)
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 6
    ),
    scale_x_continuous(
      "Detection score (mean of participant means)",
      limits = task2_gradient_limits,
      breaks = scales::breaks_width(0.05),
      labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
      # Keep the end ticks clear of the break marks.
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)
    ),
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = task2_gradient_summary$y_position,
      labels = figure_vistype(task2_gradient_summary$vistype),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 0.65))
    ),
    labs(y = NULL),
    x_axis_end_mark(side = "left"),
    x_axis_end_mark(),
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off"),
    plot_theme(base_size = 20),
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        colour = vistype_label_colours(task2_gradient_summary$vistype, other = "black")
      ),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank()
    )
  )
}
```

## Detection-score analysis

- The primary analysis uses the extended model:

  ```r
  score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)
  ```

- The outcome contains exact 0 and 1 values as well as intermediate scores. An
  ordered-beta model retains this graded information while supporting the complete closed
  interval from 0 to 1. A binary logistic model would instead treat every score below 1
  as equally incorrect.

::: {.callout-note title="What is an ordered-beta model? — Expand" collapse="true"}
An **ordered-beta model** (Kubinec, 2023) is a regression model for scores between 0
and 1 that include exact 0s and exact 1s. A plain beta model cannot handle exact 0s and
1s.

It treats each score as one of three ordered outcomes:

| Outcome | Probability | Model part |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly 0 | P(0) = 1 − logit⁻¹(η − ψ₁) | lower cutpoint ψ₁ |
| Between 0 and 1 | 1 − P(0) − P(1) | beta distribution with mean μ = logit⁻¹(η) |
| Exactly 1 | P(1) = logit⁻¹(η − ψ₂) | upper cutpoint ψ₂ |

- **One linear predictor η** (visualization, pattern, position and random effects)
  drives all three parts. A higher η makes an exact 1 more likely, an exact 0 less
  likely, and the scores in between higher. Each term therefore has a single
  coefficient: positive means better detection.
- **Coefficients** are on the logit scale, as in an ordinal logistic model.
- **Expected score:** E[y] = P(1) + (1 − P(0) − P(1)) μ. The back-transformed
  `emmeans` value is μ alone, so the expected scores below are computed from all three
  parts.

Reference: Kubinec, R. (2023). Ordered beta regression: A parsimonious, well-fitting
model for continuous data with lower and upper bounds. *Political Analysis, 31*(4),
519–536. <https://doi.org/10.1017/pan.2022.20>
:::

- Every participant completed 21 trials, so responses from the same participant are
  related. Adding `(1 | ID)` gives each participant their own baseline detection
  performance while estimating common visualization, pattern, and presentation-position
  effects.

- Some stimuli may be intrinsically easier to interpret than others. Adding
  `(1 | stimulus)` gives each stimulus its own baseline score, so visualization
  comparisons are not attributed to stimulus difficulty alone.

- Each stimulus was rendered in all seven visualizations, giving
  `r n_distinct(interaction(task2_model$stimulus, task2_model$vistype, drop = TRUE))`
  distinct images, and each image was seen by about
  `r round(mean(table(interaction(task2_model$stimulus, task2_model$vistype, drop = TRUE))))`
  participants. Adding `(1 | stimulus:vistype)`
  gives each image its own deviation from what its stimulus and visualization predict.
  Without it, the responses to one image would count as independent evidence about the
  visualization, although they share whatever made that particular image easy or hard.

- ERP pattern and centered presentation position adjust the visualization comparisons for
  the displayed pattern and for linear change as participants progressed through the task.

- The simpler base model is shown first as a reference. It contains visualization type
  and a participant random intercept but does not adjust for pattern, presentation
  position, or differences among stimuli.

```{r}
model_task2_base <- glmmTMB(
  score ~ vistype + (1 | ID),
  family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_model
)

summary(model_task2_base)$coefficients$cond |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  # Visualization terms in the display order of every figure (audit V1); the other
  # terms keep the model's order after them.
  arrange(match(term, c("(Intercept)", paste0("vistype", vistype_order)), nomatch = 99L)) |>
  transmute(
    term = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      `(Intercept)` = "Basic topoplot (intercept)",
      vistypeadjacent = "Adjacent plots vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeanimation = "Animation vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_corner = "Bivariate corner vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_range = "Bivariate range vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypetriple_CI = "Confidence intervals vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeuncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers vs Basic topoplot",
      .default = term
    ),
    estimate = Estimate,
    standard_error = .data[["Std. Error"]],
    z_value = .data[["z value"]],
    p_value = format.pval(.data[["Pr(>|z|)"]], digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",

      "Term",
```

```{r task2-position-slope}
#| include: false
# Participant-specific presentation-position slope, reported in the callout below.
model_task2_position_slope <- glmmTMB(
  score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 + position_c | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype),
  family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_model
)
task2_position_slope_converged <-
  model_task2_position_slope$fit$convergence == 0 &&
  isTRUE(model_task2_position_slope$sdr$pdHess)
task2_position_slope_sd <-
  attr(VarCorr(model_task2_position_slope)$cond$ID, "stddev")[["position_c"]]
```

::: {.callout-note title="Why correlated participant-specific visualization slopes were not retained" collapse="true"}
We tested whether the effect of visualization type differed between participants by
adding correlated participant-specific visualization effects: `(1 + vistype | ID)`.
The model could not estimate this full structure reliably:

- It ended with convergence code 1, a non-positive-definite Hessian, and singular
  convergence.

- The structure requires seven participant-level random coefficients and 28
  variance--covariance parameters.

- Each participant provided only three detection scores for each visualization type,
  which did not contain enough information to estimate all those parameters reliably.

We also tested simpler participant-specific structures:

- A participant-specific position slope, `(1 + position_c | ID)`,
  `r if (task2_position_slope_converged) "converged" else "did not converge cleanly"`.
  Its estimated standard deviation was
  `r sprintf("%.3f", task2_position_slope_sd)` on the logit scale per trial,
  against a fixed position effect of
  `r sprintf("%.3f", fixef(model_task2)$cond[["position_c"]])`. Across the
  `r n_distinct(task2_model$position_c) - 1` steps from the first to the last trial, one
  slope SD amounts to
  `r sprintf("%.2f", task2_position_slope_sd * (n_distinct(task2_model$position_c) - 1))`
  logit units.

- A diagonal visualization structure, `diag(0 + vistype | ID)`, which estimates separate
  participant-specific visualization variances without their correlations, was tried
  during model building. It is not refitted on this page, so no result from it is
  reported here.

We therefore retained participant, stimulus and image random intercepts in the primary model.
This does not show that visualization effects are identical for every participant. It
means that these data cannot reliably estimate the full correlated structure.
:::

```{r}
model_table_note(
```

### Model-estimated detection scores {#expected-detection-scores}

- The ordered-beta model has three parts: the probability of an exact 0, the
  probability of an exact 1, and the mean μ of the continuous scores in between. The
  back-transformed estimated marginal mean from `emmeans(type = "response")` is μ only,
  so it ignores the exact 0s and 1s.

- The expected score combines all three parts:
  E[y] = P(1) + (1 − P(0) − P(1)) μ, where P(0) and P(1) follow from the model's two
  cutpoints. Because
  `r round(100 * mean(task2_model$score == 1))`% of the responses are exact 1s, E[y]
  is noticeably higher than μ.

- E[y] is reported in two forms:
  - **Averaged over participants, stimuli and images** (primary). The random intercepts
    are integrated out, so this is the expected score of a new participant on a new
    stimulus. It is directly comparable with observed means.
  - **Typical participant, stimulus and image** (random effects set to zero).

```{r task2-expected-score}
# Expected score of the ordered-beta model. glmmTMB stores the two cutpoints
# directly as the "psi" parameters: P(0) = 1 - logit^-1(eta - psi1),
# P(1) = logit^-1(eta - psi2).
task2_expected_score <- function(eta, cut_zero, cut_one) {
  p_zero <- 1 - plogis(eta - cut_zero)
  p_one <- plogis(eta - cut_one)
  p_one + (1 - p_zero - p_one) * plogis(eta)
}

task2_grid <- ref_grid(model_task2, at = list(position_c = 0))
task2_grid_x <- task2_grid@linfct
task2_grid_rows <- task2_grid@grid

task2_par <- model_task2$fit$par
task2_par_cov <- model_task2$sdr$cov.fixed
task2_is_beta <- names(task2_par) == "beta"
task2_is_theta <- names(task2_par) == "theta"
task2_is_psi <- names(task2_par) == "psi"

stopifnot(
  ncol(task2_grid_x) == sum(task2_is_beta),
  sum(task2_is_psi) == 2,
  # All random effects are scalar intercepts, so their sum is normal with the
  # summed variance.
  sum(task2_is_theta) == 3
)

# Quadrature nodes for averaging over the summed random intercepts.
task2_re_nodes <- qnorm((seq_len(201) - 0.5) / 201)

task2_expected_from_par <- function(par) {
  eta <- drop(task2_grid_x %*% par[task2_is_beta])
  cuts <- par[task2_is_psi]
  re_sd <- sqrt(sum(exp(2 * par[task2_is_theta])))
  tibble::tibble(
    vistype = task2_grid_rows$vistype,
    conditional = task2_expected_score(eta, cuts[1], cuts[2]),
    marginal = rowMeans(task2_expected_score(
      outer(eta, re_sd * task2_re_nodes, `+`),
      cuts[1],
      cuts[2]
    ))
  ) |>
    group_by(vistype) |>
    summarise(across(c(conditional, marginal), mean), .groups = "drop")
}

task2_expected_point <- task2_expected_from_par(task2_par)

set.seed(20261118)
task2_expected_n_draws <- 4000
task2_par_draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(task2_expected_n_draws, task2_par, task2_par_cov)
task2_expected_draws <- purrr::map_dfr(
  seq_len(task2_expected_n_draws),
  \(i) task2_expected_from_par(task2_par_draws[i, ]) |> mutate(draw = i)
)

task2_observed_means <- task2_model |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(observed = mean(score), .groups = "drop") |>
  (\(x) setNames(x$observed, as.character(x$vistype)))()

task2_mu_basic <- emmeans(
  model_task2, ~vistype, at = list(position_c = 0), type = "response"
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(vistype == "basic") |>
  pull(response)

task2_expected_summary <- task2_expected_draws |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    conditional_lower = quantile(conditional, 0.025),
    conditional_upper = quantile(conditional, 0.975),
    marginal_lower = quantile(marginal, 0.025),
    marginal_upper = quantile(marginal, 0.975),
    marginal_lower_99 = quantile(marginal, 0.005),
    marginal_upper_99 = quantile(marginal, 0.995),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(task2_expected_point, by = "vistype") |>
  mutate(observed = unname(task2_observed_means[as.character(vistype)]))

task2_expected_value <- function(vistype, form) {
  task2_expected_point[[form]][task2_expected_point$vistype == vistype]
}

# Object used by the estimate figure: primary (averaged) expected score.
task2_estimates <- task2_expected_summary |>
  transmute(
    vistype = as.character(vistype),
    predicted_score = marginal,
    lower_ci = marginal_lower,
    upper_ci = marginal_upper,
    lower_99 = marginal_lower_99,
    upper_99 = marginal_upper_99
  ) |>
  # Rows in the display order of every figure (audit V1), Basic topoplot at the top
  # of the horizontal figure.
  mutate(vistype = order_vistype(vistype, top_first = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(vistype)

task2_expected_summary |>
  arrange(order_vistype(vistype)) |>
  transmute(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    marginal = sprintf(
      "%.1f%% [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]",
      100 * marginal, 100 * marginal_lower, 100 * marginal_upper
    ),
    conditional = sprintf(
      "%.1f%% [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]",
      100 * conditional, 100 * conditional_lower, 100 * conditional_upper
    ),
    observed = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * observed)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Expected score, averaged over random effects [95% CI]",
      "Expected score, random effects at zero [95% CI]",
      "Observed mean score"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Model-estimated expected detection scores E[y] by visualization type.",
      "Intervals are pointwise (not adjusted for multiplicity)."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Ordered-beta mixed model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + ",
    "(1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Estimand:</strong> E[y] = P(1) + (1 &minus; P(0) &minus; P(1)) &mu;, ",
    "including the probability of exact 0 and 1 scores.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Averaged over random effects:</strong> participant, stimulus and ",
    "image intercepts integrated out (expected score of a new participant on a new ",
    "stimulus).</li>",
    "<li><strong>Random effects at zero:</strong> a typical participant, stimulus ",
    "and image.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Presentation position and pattern:</strong> position 11; MMN, N170 ",
    "and P3 weighted equally.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Intervals:</strong> 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of ",
    scales::comma(task2_expected_n_draws),
    " parameter draws.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

- Both forms are evaluated at the middle presentation position (`position_c = 0`) and
  averaged with equal weight over MMN, N170 and P3. 95% intervals come from
  `r scales::comma(task2_expected_n_draws)` draws of all fixed parameters (coefficients,
  cutpoints and random-effect standard deviations) from their estimated joint sampling
  distribution.

- For Basic topoplot, μ is
  `r scales::percent(task2_mu_basic, accuracy = 0.1)`, E[y] at random effects of zero
  is `r scales::percent(task2_expected_value("basic", "conditional"), accuracy = 0.1)`,
  E[y] averaged over random effects is
  `r scales::percent(task2_expected_value("basic", "marginal"), accuracy = 0.1)`, and the
  observed mean is `r scales::percent(task2_observed_means[["basic"]], accuracy = 0.1)`.

### Tests vs Basic topoplot {#primary-comparisons-each-visualization-versus-basic-topoplot}

- **Primary family.** The six comparisons of each visualization with Basic topoplot
  form one family. P values and intervals are adjusted for these six comparisons with
  Dunnett's method. The same adjustment is used in the table and the figure.

- **Tests and intervals.** The test is the logit-scale contrast of the estimated
  marginal means. Because the expected score increases monotonically with the linear
  predictor, this test also applies to the difference in expected scores. Intervals for
  the expected-score difference are simultaneous 95% intervals from the parameter draws.

```{r task2-basic-contrasts}
emm_task2 <- emmeans(
  model_task2,
  ~ vistype,
  at = list(position_c = 0)
)

set.seed(20261118)
task2_dunnett <- contrast(
  emm_task2,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = "basic",
  adjust = "mvt"
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"))

# Expected-score differences from Basic, averaged over random effects, with
# simultaneous (max-|z|) 95% intervals across the six comparisons.
task2_other_vistypes <- setdiff(levels(task2_model$vistype), "basic")
task2_expected_wide <- task2_expected_draws |>
  select(draw, vistype, marginal) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = vistype, values_from = marginal)
task2_difference_draws <- sapply(
  task2_other_vistypes,
  \(v) task2_expected_wide[[v]] - task2_expected_wide[["basic"]]
)
task2_difference_sd <- apply(task2_difference_draws, 2, sd)
task2_difference_crit <- quantile(
  apply(
    abs(sweep(
      sweep(task2_difference_draws, 2, colMeans(task2_difference_draws)),
      2,
      task2_difference_sd,
      "/"
    )),
    1,
    max
  ),
  0.95
)

task2_basic_contrasts <- tibble::tibble(
  vistype = task2_other_vistypes,
  difference = sapply(
    task2_other_vistypes,
    \(v) task2_expected_value(v, "marginal") - task2_expected_value("basic", "marginal")
  ),
  lower_ci = difference - task2_difference_crit * task2_difference_sd,
  upper_ci = difference + task2_difference_crit * task2_difference_sd
) |>
  left_join(
    task2_dunnett |> select(vistype, logit_difference = estimate, SE, z.ratio, p.value),
    by = "vistype"
  ) |>
  # Display order of every figure and table (audit V1); the contrast figure
  # reverses it so that the first row is at the top.
  mutate(vistype = order_vistype(vistype))

task2_dunnett_significant <- task2_basic_contrasts |> filter(p.value < 0.05)
task2_corner <- task2_basic_contrasts |> filter(vistype == "bivariate_corner")
task2_dunnett_sentence <- if (nrow(task2_dunnett_significant) == 0) {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "No visualization differed from Basic topoplot after Dunnett adjustment",
      "(smallest adjusted p = %s). The largest difference was for %s: %+.1f",
      "percentage points [%+.1f, %+.1f]."
    ),
    sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", min(task2_basic_contrasts$p.value))),
    table_vistype(task2_basic_contrasts$vistype[which.max(abs(task2_basic_contrasts$difference))]),
    100 * task2_basic_contrasts$difference[which.max(abs(task2_basic_contrasts$difference))],
    100 * task2_basic_contrasts$lower_ci[which.max(abs(task2_basic_contrasts$difference))],
    100 * task2_basic_contrasts$upper_ci[which.max(abs(task2_basic_contrasts$difference))]
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "After Dunnett adjustment, ",
    paste(
      sprintf(
        "%s differed from Basic topoplot (%+.1f percentage points [%+.1f, %+.1f], adjusted p = %s)",
        table_vistype(task2_dunnett_significant$vistype),
        100 * task2_dunnett_significant$difference,
        100 * task2_dunnett_significant$lower_ci,
        100 * task2_dunnett_significant$upper_ci,
        sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", task2_dunnett_significant$p.value))
      ),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    ". No other visualization differed from Basic topoplot."
  )
}

task2_basic_contrasts |>
  arrange(vistype) |>
  transmute(
    vistype = paste(table_vistype(vistype), "vs Basic topoplot"),
    difference = sprintf(
      "%+.1f [%+.1f, %+.1f]",
      100 * difference, 100 * lower_ci, 100 * upper_ci
    ),
    logit_difference,
    SE,
    z.ratio,
    p.value = format_pvalue_html(p.value)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Comparison",
      "Expected-score difference, pp [simultaneous 95% CI]",
      "Difference (logit scale)",
      "SE",
      "z ratio",
      "Dunnett-adjusted p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Primary comparisons: each visualization versus Basic topoplot, Dunnett-adjusted",
      "for six comparisons. Values with adjusted p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Ordered-beta mixed model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + ",
    "(1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Expected-score difference:</strong> E[y] averaged over random ",
    "effects, in percentage points (pp), with simultaneous 95% intervals for the six ",
    "comparisons (max-|z| critical value ",
    sprintf("%.2f", task2_difference_crit),
    " from the parameter draws).</li>",
    "<li><strong>Test:</strong> logit-scale contrast of estimated marginal means at ",
    "position 11, patterns weighted equally; p values use the Dunnett (multivariate ",
    "t) adjustment for six comparisons with a common reference.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

**Result.** `r task2_dunnett_sentence`

::: {.callout-note title="Secondary (exploratory): all pairwise comparisons, Tukey-adjusted" collapse="true"}

These 21 pairwise comparisons are exploratory and are not part of the primary family.
They use a different adjustment (Tukey, for 21 comparisons), so their p values for the
comparisons with Basic topoplot are larger than the primary Dunnett-adjusted values.

**Why Tukey and not Dunnett.** Dunnett adjusts comparisons with one reference (here,
the six visualizations against Basic). These comparisons have no single reference: every
visualization is compared with every other. Tukey is the standard adjustment for all
pairs. Its intervals are wider, because it accounts for 21 comparisons instead of 6.

```{r task2-pairwise-comparisons}
task2_pairs <- pairs(
  emm_task2,
  adjust = "tukey"
)

task2_pairs |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    contrast = table_contrast(contrast),
    p.value = format_pvalue_html(p.value)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Comparison",
      "Difference (logit scale)",
      "SE",
      "df",
      "z ratio",
      "Tukey-adjusted p value"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Secondary, exploratory: Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons of detection scores.",
      "Values with adjusted p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Ordered-beta mixed model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + ",
    "(1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Comparison scale:</strong> Estimated marginal means were compared ",
    "on the logit scale.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Presentation position:</strong> Position 11.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Pattern averaging:</strong> Patterns received equal weight.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Multiple comparisons:</strong> Tukey adjustment for all 21 pairs ",
    "(exploratory family).</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

:::

**Figure method.** The points are expected detection scores E[y] from the extended
ordered-beta mixed model
`score ~ visualization type + pattern + centered position + (1 | participant) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | image)`,
fitted with a logit link. E[y] includes the probability of exact 0 and 1 scores and is
averaged over the participant, stimulus and image random intercepts. It is evaluated at
the middle presentation position (`position_c = 0`, corresponding to position 11) and
averaged equally over the MMN, N170, and P3 patterns. Error bars are pointwise 95%
intervals from the parameter draws.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Ambiguation

```{r task2-estimate-ambiguation}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "Expected detection score E[y] of each visualization, averaged over participants, stimuli and images. Dark band: pointwise 95% confidence interval; light ends: 99%; white tick: estimate. Both intervals from the same 4,000 parameter draws."
#| fig-alt: "Two-tone bands of expected detection score for the seven visualizations, all between about 65% and 78%, overlapping; Basic topoplot at 71%."

# Two-tone version of the estimate figure (ambiguation, Gschwandtner et al.
# 2016, Fig. 1f): dark band = pointwise 95% interval, light ends = 99%, white
# tick = estimate. The figure used on the Summary page.
make_estimate_ambiguation_figure <- function(estimates, estimate, x_title, print = FALSE) {
  s <- interval_figure_sizes(print)
  d <- estimates |>
    transmute(
      vistype, prob = {{ estimate }}, lower_95 = lower_ci, upper_95 = upper_ci,
      lower_99, upper_99, y_position = as.numeric(vistype)
    ) |>
    # Bottom row first, so the label colours below match the axis breaks.
    arrange(y_position)
  limits <- c(floor(min(d$lower_99) / 0.05) * 0.05, ceiling(max(d$upper_99) / 0.05) * 0.05)
  band <- if (print) 0.28 else 0.31
  source("scripts/ambiguation_plot.R", local = TRUE)
  plot_ambiguation_intervals(d) +
    geom_segment(
      aes(x = prob, xend = prob, y = y_position - band * 0.65, yend = y_position + band * 0.65),
      colour = "white", linewidth = s$line * 1.4
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = prob, y = y_position + band + 0.08, label = scales::percent(prob, accuracy = 1)),
      vjust = 0, size = s$label
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      x_title,
      limits = limits,
      breaks = scales::breaks_width(0.05),
      labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = d$y_position,
      labels = figure_vistype(d$vistype),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 0.7))
    ) +
    labs(y = NULL) +
    x_axis_end_mark(s$base, size = if (print) 0.55 else 1, side = "left") +
    x_axis_end_mark(s$base, size = if (print) 0.55 else 1) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    plot_theme(base_size = s$base) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        size = s$axis_y,
        colour = vistype_label_colours(as.character(d$vistype)),
        margin = margin(r = s$margin)
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = s$axis_x),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank()
    )
}
```

### Differences vs Basic topoplot {#detection-score-differences-relative-to-basic-topoplot}

**Figure method.** The contrasts are the primary comparisons from the table above:
differences in expected score E[y] (averaged over random effects) between each
visualization and Basic topoplot. The intervals are simultaneous 95% intervals for the
six comparisons, matching the Dunnett adjustment of the p values. An interval crossing
zero indicates that the visualization is not clearly different from Basic at the
familywise 95% confidence level.

```{r task2-basic-contrast-figure}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "Difference in expected detection score E[y] of each visualization from Basic topoplot, averaged over participants, stimuli and images. Bars: Dunnett-adjusted simultaneous 95% confidence intervals for the six comparisons. Dashed line: no difference."
task2_contrast_limit <- max(
  abs(c(task2_basic_contrasts$lower_ci, task2_basic_contrasts$upper_ci)),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
task2_contrast_limit <- max(
  0.05,
  ceiling(task2_contrast_limit / 0.05) * 0.05
)

# Site version, or with print = TRUE the print version (audit V7).
make_detection_score_contrast_figure <- function(print = FALSE) {
  s <- interval_figure_sizes(print)
  plot <- ggplot(
    # Adjacent plots, the first row of the display order, at the top.
    mutate(task2_basic_contrasts, vistype = order_vistype(vistype, top_first = TRUE)),
    aes(x = difference, y = vistype)
  ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = if (print) s$line else 0.6,
      colour = "#377EB8"
    ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.14,
      linewidth = s$line,
      colour = "#333333"
    ) +
    geom_point(size = s$point, colour = "#333333") +
    geom_text(
      # Beside the point, on the side away from zero (no overlap with the
      # dashed zero line).
      aes(hjust = side_away_from_zero(difference), label = ifelse(
        abs(difference) < 0.005,
        "0 pp",
        sprintf("%+.0f pp", 100 * difference)
      )),
      nudge_y = 0.32,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = s$label,
      colour = "#333333"
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(
      labels = figure_vistype,
      expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(-task2_contrast_limit, task2_contrast_limit),
      labels = function(x) ifelse(
        abs(x) < 0.005,
        "0 pp",
        sprintf("%+.0f pp", 100 * x)
      ),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.04)
    ) +
    # No in-figure title or subtitle (Wilke ch. 22): the caption defines the
    # intervals.
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    plot_theme(base_size = s$base) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = s$axis_y, margin = margin(r = s$margin)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = s$axis_x),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank()
    )

  # Axis caption with Basic topoplot in its accent colour.
  plot /
    basic_axis_caption("Difference in expected detection score vs", size = s$caption) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.10))
}
```

## Exact-peak sensitivity analysis {#sensitivity-analysis-exact-peak-responses}

- About `r round(100 * mean(task2_model$score == 1))`% of responses have a score of
  exactly 1. Scores are rescaled within each stimulus, so a score of 1 marks the strongest
  region (`r sum(table(region_scores$stimulus[region_scores$score == 1]) > 1)` stimulus
  has two regions tied at 1.00 after rounding to two decimals): these responses are trials
  in which the participant selected the strongest region. The remaining scores describe how
  close a miss was.

- The ordered-beta model handles exact 0 and 1 values, but one linear predictor drives
  both the probability of a 1 and the location of intermediate scores. A visualization
  that helps participants find the exact peak without improving near misses (or the
  reverse) would therefore be averaged into a single effect.

- Two checks address this:
  1. **Posterior predictive check.** Data sets are simulated from the fitted
     ordered-beta model and compared with the observed share of exact-peak responses.
  2. **Two-part model.** A logistic model for finding the exact peak and a beta model for
     the scores of the remaining trials, each with the same predictors and random effects
     as the primary model. Effects in the two parts that differ in direction or strength
     indicate that the single-predictor ordered-beta contrast summarizes two distinct
     effects.

### Posterior predictive check

```{r task2-peak-ppc}
set.seed(20261116)
task2_peak_n_sim <- 1000
task2_peak_sims <- simulate(model_task2, nsim = task2_peak_n_sim)

task2_peak_stats <- function(score, vistype) {
  per_vistype <- tibble::tibble(vistype = vistype, score = score) |>
    group_by(vistype) |>
    summarise(
      share_one = mean(score == 1),
      mean_score = mean(score),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  basic <- per_vistype[per_vistype$vistype == "basic", ]
  per_vistype |>
    mutate(
      share_one_vs_basic = share_one - basic$share_one,
      mean_score_vs_basic = mean_score - basic$mean_score
    )
}

task2_peak_observed <- task2_peak_stats(task2_model$score, task2_model$vistype)

task2_peak_simulated <- purrr::map_dfr(
  task2_peak_sims,
  \(score) task2_peak_stats(score, task2_model$vistype),
  .id = "simulation"
)

task2_peak_ppc <- task2_peak_simulated |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    c(share_one, share_one_vs_basic, mean_score, mean_score_vs_basic),
    names_to = "statistic",
    values_to = "simulated"
  ) |>
  group_by(vistype, statistic) |>
  summarise(
    lower = quantile(simulated, 0.025),
    median = median(simulated),
    upper = quantile(simulated, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    task2_peak_observed |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-vistype, names_to = "statistic", values_to = "observed"),
    by = c("vistype", "statistic")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    inside = observed >= lower & observed <= upper,
    # Display order of every figure and table (audit V1).
    vistype = order_vistype(vistype)
  )

task2_peak_ppc |>
  filter(statistic %in% c("share_one", "share_one_vs_basic")) |>
  filter(!(statistic == "share_one_vs_basic" & vistype == "basic")) |>
  arrange(statistic, vistype) |>
  # Shares in %, differences from Basic in percentage points (signed).
  mutate(is_share = statistic == "share_one") |>
  transmute(
    statistic = if_else(
      is_share,
      "Share of exact-peak responses",
      "Difference from Basic topoplot"
    ),
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    observed = if_else(
      is_share,
      sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * observed),
      sprintf("%+.1f pp", 100 * observed)
    ),
    simulated = if_else(
      is_share,
      sprintf("%.1f%% [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]", 100 * median, 100 * lower, 100 * upper),
      sprintf(
        "%+.1f pp [%+.1f, %+.1f]",
        100 * median, 100 * lower, 100 * upper
      )
    ),
    inside = if_else(
      inside,
      "Yes",
      '<span style="color:#B2182B;font-weight:700">No</span>'
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Statistic",
      "Visualization",
      "Observed",
      "Simulated median [95% interval]",
      "Observed inside interval"
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "Observed versus simulated exact-peak responses (",
      task2_peak_n_sim,
      " data sets simulated from the primary ordered-beta model, ",
      "with new participant and stimulus effects in each simulation)."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

```{r task2-peak-ppc-figure}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-alt: "Observed share of exact-peak responses for each visualization compared with 95% intervals simulated from the ordered-beta model, shown as levels and as differences from Basic topoplot."
# Two panels instead of one free-x facet, so each gets its own unit: the share
# panel is in %, the difference panel in percentage points (audit V10). Same look
# as a facet_wrap with a shared y axis.
task2_peak_ppc_plot_data <- task2_peak_ppc |>
  filter(statistic %in% c("share_one", "share_one_vs_basic")) |>
  filter(!(statistic == "share_one_vs_basic" & vistype == "basic")) |>
  mutate(
    # First row of the display order (Basic topoplot) at the top.
    vistype = forcats::fct_rev(vistype),
    # Factor with both levels, so the two panels share one legend.
    inside = factor(inside, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))
  )
task2_peak_ppc_rows <- rev(levels(task2_peak_ppc$vistype))

task2_peak_ppc_panel <- function(stat, title, x_labels) {
  task2_peak_ppc_plot_data |>
    filter(statistic == stat) |>
    mutate(panel = title) |>
    ggplot(aes(y = vistype)) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.25,
      linewidth = 0.8,
      colour = "#9ECAE1"
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(x = median), shape = 124, size = 5, colour = "#3182BD") +
    # show.legend = TRUE draws both keys even in a panel without a point outside
    # its interval, so the two legends are identical and collected into one.
    geom_point(aes(x = observed, fill = inside), shape = 21, size = 3.5, show.legend = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(`TRUE` = "#333333", `FALSE` = "#B2182B"),
      labels = c(`TRUE` = "Inside 95% interval", `FALSE` = "Outside 95% interval"),
      limits = c("FALSE", "TRUE"),
      name = "Observed"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = x_labels) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = figure_vistype, limits = task2_peak_ppc_rows, drop = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~panel) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    # Text sizes for the ~1100 px display width of this 11-in figure (audit V2):
    # tick labels close to the panel titles, so neither looks tiny or oversized.
    plot_theme(base_size = 18) +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        colour = vistype_label_colours(task2_peak_ppc_rows, other = "black")
      ),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 19),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 18),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 17)
    )
}

task2_peak_ppc_share_panel <- task2_peak_ppc_panel(
  "share_one",
  "Share of exact-peak responses",
  scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)
) +
  # The share axis covers only part of the 0-100% scale: double slashes at both

  x_axis_end_mark(base_size = 18, side = "left") +

task2_peak_ppc_share_panel + task2_peak_ppc_difference_panel +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = "Blue: median and 95% interval of simulated data sets. Dots: observed values.",
    theme = theme(

      )
    )
```

### Two-part model for hits and misses {#two-part-model}

- **Exact peak:** logistic mixed model for `score == 1`.
- **Closeness of misses:** beta mixed model for the trials with `score < 1`. The
  `r sum(task2_model$score == 0)` scores of exactly 0 were moved slightly inward with the
  Smithson–Verkuilen transformation, `(score × (n − 1) + 0.5) / n`.
- Both parts use the primary model's predictors:
  `vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)`.
- The second part is conditional on missing the peak. If a visualization turns near
  misses into exact hits, its remaining misses can look worse even when overall
  performance improves, so the two parts should be read together.

```{r task2-peak-two-part}
task2_peak_hit_model <- glmmTMB(
  peak ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype),
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = mutate(task2_model, peak = as.integer(score == 1))
)

task2_peak_miss_data <- task2_model |>
  filter(score < 1) |>
  mutate(score_squeezed = (score * (n() - 1) + 0.5) / n())

task2_peak_miss_model <- glmmTMB(
  score_squeezed ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype),
  family = beta_family(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_peak_miss_data
)

stopifnot(
  task2_peak_hit_model$fit$convergence == 0,
  isTRUE(task2_peak_hit_model$sdr$pdHess),
  task2_peak_miss_model$fit$convergence == 0,
  isTRUE(task2_peak_miss_model$sdr$pdHess)
)

# Overall test of visualization type in each part: likelihood-ratio test against
# the same model without vistype (as on the Hit or miss page).
task2_peak_overall <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  list(`Exact peak` = task2_peak_hit_model, `Misses` = task2_peak_miss_model),
  \(model, name) {
    reduced <- update(model, . ~ . - vistype)
    chi <- as.numeric(2 * (logLik(model) - logLik(reduced)))
    df <- attr(logLik(model), "df") - attr(logLik(reduced), "df")
    tibble::tibble(part = name, chi = chi, df = df,
                   p = pchisq(chi, df, lower.tail = FALSE))
  }
)
task2_peak_overall_text <- function(name) {
  r <- task2_peak_overall[task2_peak_overall$part == name, ]
  sprintf("χ²(%d) = %.1f, p = %.2f", r$df, r$chi, r$p)
}

# Averaged over participants, stimuli and images (random intercepts integrated
# out), as for E[y]; see marginal_response_by_vistype().
task2_peak_response_estimates <- bind_rows(
  `Probability of exact peak` = marginal_response_by_vistype(task2_peak_hit_model),
  `Mean score of misses` = marginal_response_by_vistype(task2_peak_miss_model),
  .id = "part"
)

task2_peak_response_estimates |>
  arrange(order_vistype(vistype)) |>
  transmute(
    part,
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    value = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", marginal, marginal_lower, marginal_upper)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = value) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization",
      "Probability of exact peak [95% CI]",
      "Mean score of misses [95% CI]"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Model-estimated values from the two-part model, averaged equally over ERP",
      "patterns at the middle presentation position and over participants, stimuli",
      "and images (random intercepts integrated out). Intervals: 4,000 draws of the",
      "model parameters."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

**Overall test of visualization type** (likelihood ratio against the same model without
it): exact peak `r task2_peak_overall_text("Exact peak")`; misses
`r task2_peak_overall_text("Misses")`. When the overall test is not significant, read the
single comparisons with Basic below as exploratory.

### Visualization effects by model {#visualization-effects-across-models}

```{r task2-peak-contrasts}
task2_peak_contrasts <- list(
  `Ordered beta (primary)` = model_task2,
  `Exact peak (logistic)` = task2_peak_hit_model,
  `Misses (beta)` = task2_peak_miss_model
) |>
  purrr::imap_dfr(\(model, name) {
    set.seed(20261118)
    emmeans(model, ~vistype, at = list(position_c = 0)) |>
      contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "basic", adjust = "mvt") |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        model = name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        estimate,
        lower = asymp.LCL,
        upper = asymp.UCL
      )
  }) |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = unique(model)),
    # Display order of every figure and table (audit V1).
    vistype = order_vistype(vistype),
    excludes_zero = lower > 0 | upper < 0
  )

task2_peak_contrasts |>
  arrange(vistype) |>
  transmute(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    model,
    value = if_else(
      excludes_zero,
      sprintf(
        '<span style="color:#B2182B;font-weight:700">%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]</span>',
        estimate, lower, upper
      ),
      sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", estimate, lower, upper)
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = value) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Visualization vs Basic topoplot", levels(task2_peak_contrasts$model)),
    caption = paste(
      "Differences from Basic topoplot on the logit scale with Dunnett-adjusted 95%",
      "confidence intervals (six comparisons within each model, as in the primary",
      "analysis). Intervals excluding zero are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Scale:</strong> All three columns are on the logit scale: the ",
    "logit of the mean score (ordered beta and misses) or the log-odds of selecting ",
    "the strongest region (exact peak). Directions are comparable; magnitudes are ",
    "not directly comparable across columns.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Multiplicity:</strong> Within each model, intervals are ",
    "Dunnett-adjusted for the six comparisons with Basic topoplot, the same family ",
    "as the primary analysis.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Reading the table"
)
```

```{r task2-peak-contrast-figure}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-alt: "Differences from Basic topoplot on the logit scale for the ordered-beta model, the exact-peak logistic model, and the beta model of missed trials, with 95% confidence intervals."
# Rows in the display order of every figure (audit V1), as in the detection-score
# contrast figure: Adjacent plots at the top. Basic topoplot is the reference and
# has no row.
task2_peak_contrast_plot <- task2_peak_contrasts |>
  mutate(vistype = order_vistype(vistype, top_first = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = vistype)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = basic_accent) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper, colour = excludes_zero),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.2,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  # Neutral encoding as in the rating contrast figure (audit V17c, V17d): filled
  # dark point = interval excludes zero, open grey point = includes zero. No red.
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = excludes_zero, shape = excludes_zero),
    fill = "white",
    size = 3.45,
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 21, `TRUE` = 19), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = "#8C8C8C", `TRUE` = "#222222"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = figure_vistype) +
  facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  # Text sizes for the ~1100 px display width of this 12-in figure (audit V2).
  plot_theme(base_size = 19) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 19),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20)
  )

# Axis caption as in the main contrast figures, with Basic topoplot in its accent.
task2_peak_contrast_plot /
  basic_axis_caption("Difference (logit scale) from", size = 20) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.08)) +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = paste(
      "Filled points: Dunnett-adjusted 95% confidence interval excludes zero;",
      "open grey points: interval includes zero."
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(

      )
```

```{r task2-peak-agreement}
task2_peak_agreement <- task2_peak_contrasts |>
  mutate(
    part = case_when(
      model == "Ordered beta (primary)" ~ "primary",
      model == "Exact peak (logistic)" ~ "peak",
      TRUE ~ "miss"
    ),
    direction = case_when(
      !excludes_zero ~ "none",
      estimate > 0 ~ "better",
      TRUE ~ "worse"
    )
  ) |>
  select(vistype, part, direction, estimate) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = c(direction, estimate)) |>
  rename(primary = direction_primary, peak = direction_peak, miss = direction_miss) |>
  mutate(
    pattern = case_when(
      peak == "none" & miss == "none" ~ "No clear effect in either part",
      peak != "none" & miss != "none" & peak != miss ~
        "Opposite effects on exact peak and misses",
      peak != "none" & miss != "none" ~ "Same effect in both parts",
      peak != "none" ~ paste0(
        "Exact peak only (", if_else(peak == "better", "more", "fewer"), " exact hits)"
      ),
      TRUE ~ paste0(
        "Misses only (", if_else(miss == "better", "closer", "farther"), " misses)"
      )
    ),
    primary_captures = case_when(
      primary == "none" & (peak != "none" | miss != "none") ~
        "No: the ordered-beta contrast shows no clear effect",
      primary != "none" & peak != "none" & peak != primary ~
        "Partly: the exact-peak effect has the opposite direction",
      primary != "none" &
        sign(estimate_peak) != sign(estimate_primary) ~
        "Partly: the exact-peak estimate points the other way (interval includes zero)",
      primary != "none" &
        sign(estimate_miss) != sign(estimate_primary) ~
        "Partly: the miss estimate points the other way (interval includes zero)",
      TRUE ~ "Yes"
    )
  )

task2_peak_agreement |>
  arrange(vistype) |>
  transmute(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    pattern,
    primary_captures = if_else(
      primary_captures == "Yes",
      "Yes",
      paste0('<span style="color:#B2182B;font-weight:700">', primary_captures, "</span>")
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization vs Basic topoplot",
      "Two-part model",
      "Captured by the primary ordered-beta contrast?"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Agreement between the two-part model and the primary model. An effect counts",
      "when its Dunnett-adjusted 95% confidence interval excludes zero."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

## Rank and top-3 sensitivity analysis {#sensitivity-analysis-rank-and-top-3-outcomes}

```{r task2-rank-data}
# Rank of every region within its stimulus by score (1 = strongest region).
task2_region_ranks <- region_scores |>
  group_by(stimulus) |>
  mutate(
    rank_average = rank(-score, ties.method = "average"),
    rank_min = rank(-score, ties.method = "min"),
    n_regions = n()
  ) |>
  ungroup()

task2_tenth_best <- task2_region_ranks |>
  filter(rank_min == 10)

# task2_model keeps the row order of task2 (no rows are dropped, checked above),
# so the selected region can be attached by position.
stopifnot(identical(as.character(task2_model$stimulus), as.character(task2$stimulus)))

task2_rank_model_data <- task2_model |>
  mutate(region = task2$region) |>
  left_join(
    task2_region_ranks |> select(stimulus, region, rank_average, rank_min, n_regions),
    by = c("stimulus", "region")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # 1 = strongest region, 0 = weakest; ties share their average rank.
    rank_score = (n_regions - rank_average) / (n_regions - 1),
    top3 = as.integer(rank_min <= 3)
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(task2_rank_model_data) == nrow(task2_model),
  !anyNA(task2_rank_model_data$rank_score)
)

# Most frequently selected region for each stimulus and its rank by score.
task2_modal_regions <- task2_rank_model_data |>
  count(pattern, stimulus, region, rank_min, score, name = "responses") |>
  group_by(stimulus) |>
  slice_max(responses, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

task2_p3_low_modal <- task2_modal_regions |>
  filter(pattern == "P3", rank_min > 3)
task2_p3_low_modal_top_region <- names(which.max(table(task2_p3_low_modal$region)))
task2_p3_low_modal_top_region_n <- max(table(task2_p3_low_modal$region))
task2_p3_low_modal_top_ranks <- task2_p3_low_modal |>
  filter(region == task2_p3_low_modal_top_region) |>
  pull(rank_min)
```

- **Why a sensitivity analysis.** Region values are min–max rescaled within each
  stimulus, so the same score does not mean the same thing for different stimuli. For
  example, the 10th-strongest region has a score between
  `r sprintf("%.2f", min(task2_tenth_best$score))` and
  `r sprintf("%.2f", max(task2_tenth_best$score))`, depending on the stimulus. Score
  magnitudes, and differences between them, should therefore not be compared across
  stimuli. The visualization comparisons are within stimuli (every stimulus is shown in
  every visualization), but the score scale still weights a miss differently for
  different stimuli.

- **Two outcomes that do not depend on the score scale.**
  - **Rank score:** the rank of the selected region among the
    `r task2_region_ranks$n_regions[1]` regions of its stimulus, mapped to 0–1
    (1 = strongest region, 0 = weakest; tied regions share their average rank).
    Modelled with the same ordered-beta model as the primary analysis.
  - **Top 3:** whether the selected region is among the three strongest regions of its
    stimulus (`r scales::percent(mean(task2_rank_model_data$top3), accuracy = 1)` of
    responses). Modelled with a logistic mixed model.
  - Both models use the primary predictors and random effects:
    `vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype)`.

```{r task2-rank-models}
task2_rank_model <- glmmTMB(
  rank_score ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype),
  family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_rank_model_data
)

task2_top3_model <- glmmTMB(
  top3 ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | stimulus:vistype),
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = task2_rank_model_data
)

stopifnot(
  task2_rank_model$fit$convergence == 0,
  isTRUE(task2_rank_model$sdr$pdHess),
  task2_top3_model$fit$convergence == 0,
  isTRUE(task2_top3_model$sdr$pdHess)
)

task2_outcome_contrasts <- list(
  `Score (primary)` = model_task2,
  `Rank score` = task2_rank_model,
  `Top 3` = task2_top3_model
) |>
  purrr::imap_dfr(\(model, name) {
    set.seed(20261118)
    emmeans(model, ~vistype, at = list(position_c = 0)) |>
      contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "basic", adjust = "mvt") |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        outcome = name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        estimate,
        SE,
        p.value
      )
  }) |>
  mutate(
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = unique(outcome)),
    # Display order of every figure and table (audit V1).
    vistype = order_vistype(vistype)
  )

task2_outcome_contrasts |>
  arrange(vistype) |>
  transmute(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    outcome,
    value = if_else(
      p.value < 0.05,
      sprintf(
        '<span style="color:#B2182B;font-weight:700">%+.2f (p = %s)</span>',
        estimate, sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
      ),
      sprintf("%+.2f (p = %s)", estimate, sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p.value)))
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = value) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Visualization vs Basic topoplot", levels(task2_outcome_contrasts$outcome)),
    caption = paste(
      "Differences from Basic topoplot on the logit scale for the primary score and the",
      "two scale-free outcomes, with Dunnett-adjusted p values (six comparisons within",
      "each outcome). Adjusted p < .05 is shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

task2_outcome_significant <- task2_outcome_contrasts |>
  filter(p.value < 0.05)
task2_outcome_sentence <- function(outcome_name) {
  hits <- task2_outcome_significant |> filter(outcome == outcome_name)
  if (nrow(hits) == 0) {
    "no visualization differed from Basic topoplot after Dunnett adjustment"
  } else {
    paste0(
      paste(
        sprintf(
          "%s differed from Basic topoplot (%+.2f logit, adjusted p = %s)",
          table_vistype(hits$vistype),
          hits$estimate,
          sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", hits$p.value))
        ),
        collapse = "; "
      )
    )
  }
}
task2_corner_by_outcome <- task2_outcome_contrasts |>
  filter(vistype == "bivariate_corner")
```

- **Result.** `r if (!any(task2_outcome_significant$outcome %in% c("Rank score", "Top 3"))) "For neither scale-free outcome did any visualization differ from Basic topoplot after Dunnett adjustment" else paste0("For the rank score, ", task2_outcome_sentence("Rank score"), "; for top 3, ", task2_outcome_sentence("Top 3"))`.
  For Bivariate corner versus Basic topoplot, the
  logit-scale estimates were
  `r sprintf("%+.2f", task2_corner_by_outcome$estimate[task2_corner_by_outcome$outcome == "Score (primary)"])`
  for the score,
  `r sprintf("%+.2f", task2_corner_by_outcome$estimate[task2_corner_by_outcome$outcome == "Rank score"])`
  for the rank score (adjusted p =
  `r sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", task2_corner_by_outcome$p.value[task2_corner_by_outcome$outcome == "Rank score"]))`)
  and
  `r sprintf("%+.2f", task2_corner_by_outcome$estimate[task2_corner_by_outcome$outcome == "Top 3"])`
  for top 3 (adjusted p =
  `r sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", task2_corner_by_outcome$p.value[task2_corner_by_outcome$outcome == "Top 3"]))`).

- **Open question about the scoring.** For
  `r task2_p3_low_modal_top_region_n` of
  `r n_distinct(task2_model$stimulus[task2_model$pattern == "P3"])` P3 stimuli, the most
  frequently selected region was `r task2_p3_low_modal_top_region`, which ranks only
  `r scales::ordinal(min(task2_p3_low_modal_top_ranks))`–`r scales::ordinal(max(task2_p3_low_modal_top_ranks))` by
  score for those stimuli. Participants may have targeted the voltage peak rather than
  the SNR peak. If so, low scores on these stimuli partly reflect how participants
  understood the task, not only how well a visualization conveyed uncertainty. This is a
  construct-validity question for the scoring and is not resolved here.

::: {.callout-note title="Most frequently selected region for each stimulus" collapse="true"}

```{r task2-modal-regions}
task2_modal_regions |>
  arrange(pattern, rank_min) |>
  transmute(
    pattern,
    stimulus,
    region,
    responses,
    rank_min,
    score = sprintf("%.2f", score)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Pattern",
      "Stimulus",
      "Most selected region",
      "Responses",
      "Rank by score (1 = strongest)",
      "Score"
    ),
    caption = "Most frequently selected region for each stimulus, with its rank by score.",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```
